method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, comparison with the already reviewed parallel propositional formation-sequence section, constructor-by-constructor replay of both directions of the equivalence proof, verification of examples, exercises and the minimality characterization, and exact structural QA after three documented frozen-source repairs. OLFOL-009 was retracted after literal macro-argument counting showed that the frozen source was already balanced. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Strings; term and formula formation sequences; equivalence with inductive formation; minimal formation sequences; and the subformula characterization.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Formation sequences give a bottom-up alternative to inductive definitions; an L-string is any finite sequence of L-symbols, so every L-formula is an L-string but not conversely.
samples.checks: The motivation, arbitrary-language scope, finite-string definition and malformed-string counterexample are all retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A term or formula formation sequence ends with its target and builds each entry only from earlier entries by the permitted constructors; examples show that order may vary and irrelevant junk may occur.
samples.checks: All term, connective and quantifier constructors, strict index inequalities, displayed examples and the informal junk explanation are preserved. The k-ary off-by-one is repaired under OLFOL-006; the target now preserves the already balanced nested Atom expression after retracting OLFOL-009.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Every inductively formed formula has a formation sequence: the atomic singleton is the base, and concatenating constituent sequences plus the new constructor gives each inductive case.
samples.checks: The atomic base and all seven constructors produce exactly the displayed terminal formula.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Initial segments of a formation sequence form their own last entry. Conversely, strong induction on sequence length shows that every string with a formula formation sequence is an inductively generated formula.
samples.checks: Both inclusions, the strong-induction hypothesis, all seven cases, the conjunction demonstration and proper-initial-subsequence argument are retained. The copied L_0 subscripts and lone equivalence symbol are repaired under OLFOL-007 and OLFOL-008.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Terms satisfy the analogous equivalence, left as an exercise with the formula proof as a hint.
samples.checks: The term set, existence condition, exercise and both references are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Minimal formation sequences have globally shortest length. A formula or term may have several such sequences but they contain the same strings, and a formula B is a subformula of A exactly when it occurs in every formation sequence, equivalently in some minimal one.
samples.checks: Both minimality clauses use the n+1 length threshold, and all three subformula conditions and exercises are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Raymond Smullyan introduced formation sequences in First-Order Logic, and Zuckerman established further properties.
samples.checks: The title, both attributions and both citation identifiers are preserved.

source_observations: The first-order section deliberately extends the parallel propositional construction with term, function and quantifier cases.
The converse theorem relies on literal string construction, so syntactic identity rather than logical equivalence is required in its conjunction case.
Three deterministic frozen-source defects are repaired adjacent to reader notes and projected back only during structural comparison; OLFOL-009 is retained only as a retracted false-positive record.
All formulas, macros, controlled tokens, identifiers, citations and references pass after the documented projections.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The compact Marathi formation-sequence terminology remains explicitly open to specialist review in T141 and T214.
